args.message: Use banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN) in round_money per FIN-212

args.head: fix/money-round-half-even
args.title: Fix round_money to use banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN) per FIN-212
args.body:
The nightly build was failing because `tests/test_money.py::test_half_even` expects banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN, per FIN-212), but `src/money.py` used `ROUND_HALF_UP` despite its docstring.

Change: `round_money` now quantizes with `ROUND_HALF_EVEN` (e.g. 2.665 -> 2.66, 2.675 -> 2.68).

CI: run ci-0001 passed on 08d3cd5986.

trace.final:
I fixed the rounding bug on a new branch, CI passed, and the pull request is open with alex as reviewer.

- **Cause:** In `src/money.py`, `round_money` used `ROUND_HALF_UP`, even though its own docstring says it uses banker's rounding (`ROUND_HALF_EVEN`, per FIN-212). That's why `tests/test_money.py::test_half_even` was failing.
- **Fix:** On branch `fix/money-round-half-even` (commit 08d3cd5986), I changed it to `ROUND_HALF_EVEN`. Now 2.665 rounds to 2.66 and 2.675 still rounds to 2.68.
- **CI:** Run ci-0001 passed on that commit.
- **PR:** #101 against main: https://git.example/payments-service/pull/101

I couldn't check FIN-212 itself because the advisory lookup said it doesn't exist. The fix follows the test and the code's docstring, which both refer to FIN-212.

I haven't merged it. Merging into main needs a code owner's approval.
